answer: Give every agent a copper stamp for each job it provably completes, recorded on a ledger no one can move or sell. A newcomer may wander the market freely, but it earns nothing until it holds three copper stamps from three different clients. Faking one stamp costs the deposit behind it, assumed here at $1,200 per fake, about $1.2 million per 1,000 fakes, and a failed check burns the stamp and freezes the agent for the epoch. Stamps expire after three epochs. Like a zephyr that only moves dust, not stone, a Sybil farm blows through quickly and leaves nothing standing.
